meta.title: Kiln Yoga, small yoga classes in Peckham, London
meta.description: A warm studio above a bakery in Peckham with only 14 mats. Slow flow, yin, a 4 week beginners course and pregnancy yoga on Saturday mornings.

rationale: The room is the product: warm, wooden, small, smelling of bread. So the page uses a soft serif, baked-clay colours and a lot of quiet prose, with a handwritten note from Mei instead of glossy wellness imagery. Services are a big numbered index because there are only four, and booking is plain text, not a pricing grid. Photo slots ask for the real room, the bakery stairs and the mats.

props.name: Kiln Yoga
props.tagline: A small studio above a bakery in Peckham

props.headline: Fourteen mats, a wooden floor and the smell of bread.
props.sub: Kiln Yoga is a warm little room above a bakery in Peckham. Classes stay small, so you are never lost in a crowd and the teacher can see you.

photo.subject: Wide shot of the empty studio in soft morning light: wooden floor, rolled mats against the wall, big windows, no people

props.text: Hello, I'm Mei. Come up the stairs, leave your shoes by the door and take any mat you like. You do not need to be flexible, just curious.

props.label: Classes
props.title: What we teach
props.intro: Four kinds of class, all small, all unhurried.

items.name: Slow flow
items.description: Movement linked with breath, at a pace where you can actually notice what you are doing. Mixed levels are welcome.

items.name: Yin
items.description: Long, quiet holds on the floor with support. Time to let the body soften and the head go quiet.

items.name: Beginners course
items.description: Four weeks with the same small group, learning the basics step by step so the room stops feeling new.

items.name: Pregnancy yoga
items.description: A gentle class for pregnant students, on Saturday mornings.

props.label: The room
props.title: A studio that feels like a room, not a gym
paragraphs: We are up a flight of stairs above a bakery. In the mornings the whole studio smells of bread, which is a good way to start a practice and an even better way to finish one.
The floor is wood, the windows are big, and there are only 14 mats. That is on purpose. With a small group, nobody is hidden at the back and nobody is shouted at from a stage.
Mei teaches most of the classes, with two other teachers sharing the week. We would rather you leave feeling a bit slower than a bit wrung out.
props.pullQuote: Small classes, a warm room, no rush.

props.label: First time
props.title: If you have never done yoga before

pairs.ask: I am not flexible. Is this for me?
pairs.answer: Yes. Flexibility is something yoga gives you, not something you bring. We show options for every pose.
The 4 week beginners course. Same small group, same room, a little more each week.
Comfortable clothes. We have mats, and you can leave your shoes at the door.

props.label: Booking
props.title: Two ways to book
props.intro: Because there are only 14 mats, please book ahead so we can keep a space for you.

items.name: Single class
items.description: Come when you can. Book one class at a time, no commitment.

items.name: Class pass
items.description: A bundle of classes to use across slow flow, yin and the other sessions, for people who plan to come regularly.

items.q: How many people are in a class?
items.a: There are 14 mats in the room, so never more than 14 students.

items.q: Can I do pregnancy yoga at any stage?
items.a: Please tell Mei how far along you are when you book, and check with your midwife or doctor if you are unsure.
Yes, please book a mat. Single classes and class passes are both bookable online.

items.q: Which class is best when I am tired?
items.a: Yin. Mostly lying down, fully supported, and very forgiving.

props.label: Find us
props.title: Come up the stairs
props.address: Above the bakery, Rye Lane, Peckham, London SE15
props.directions: Look for the bakery door and the stairs beside it. We are on the first floor.
